newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAA denies in pact to counter BA-American.
newsitem.headline: SAA denies in pact to counter BA-American.

text.p: South African Airways (SAA) on Thursday denied reports it was one of nine airlines planning an alliance to counter the threat of a proposed linkup between British Airways and American Airlines.
An SAA spokesman said the proposed BA-American Airlines venture posed no major threat to African carriers.
"We (SAA) are not part of that alliance and we are not even contemplating to join it," Jackie Rakitla told Reuters on Thursday.

Airline industry sources told Reuters in London on Wednesday that nine major carriers were planning a powerful new alliance to achieve better economies of scale and higher yileds through closer coordination.
They said carriers eyeing a counter-alliance included United Airlines, Lufthansa AG, Thai International, Brazil's Varig, SAA, Air Canada, All-Nippon Airways and British Midland.
The alliance, which sources said would be launched in mid-May, would see the frequent flyer programmes of the airlines merged.
But Rakitla said SAA had a good and longstanding partnership with American Airlines on the trans-Atlantic route between South Africa and the United States.

"The BA-American Airlines linkup does not affect African airlines and we also don't believe it will affect our European operations. It's just sheer speculation that SAA is going join this counter-alliance," he said.
"SAA has its own partneship with American Airlines where we share some flight quotas on the South African-U.S. route and it has been very good," Rakitla added.
